UsbProbe.Options.Heading: Device names
UsbProbe.Options.Explain: Vendor, product and class names come from usb.ids, the list linux-usb.org keeps. A copy ships with Nexaflow; a newer one can be downloaded and is used from then on.
UsbProbe.Options.CheckMonthly: When the USB page opens, check linux-usb.org for newer names if the last check is more than a month old
UsbProbe.Options.InUseBundled: In use: usb.ids {0}, the copy that shipped — {1:N0} vendors, {2:N0} products.
UsbProbe.Options.InUseDownloaded: In use: usb.ids {0}, downloaded — {1:N0} vendors, {2:N0} products.
UsbProbe.Options.Licence: usb.ids is downloaded from linux-usb.org and used under its BSD-3-Clause licence.
UsbProbe.Device.Page.Title: USB device
UsbProbe.Device.Toolbar.ShowInTreeTip: Open the USB page at this device
UsbProbe.Device.Toolbar.ReReadTip: Ask the device for its descriptors and strings again, waking it if it is asleep
UsbProbe.Device.Unplugged: Unplugged. Its tools have stopped; plug it back in — into any port — and this page picks it up again.
UsbProbe.Device.Structure.Name: Part
UsbProbe.Device.Tools.Ejected: Ejected: Windows has let go of it, so it can be unplugged safely. Its tools come back when it is plugged in again.
UsbProbe.Device.Tools.Hub: A hub has no live tools of its own. The devices plugged into it each have a page, with theirs — Show in USB tree lists them.
UsbProbe.Device.Tools.None: No live tool here works with this device. Interfaces shows what it is made of.
UsbProbe.Device.Tools.Uncovered: Not covered by a live tool
UsbProbe.Device.Diagnostics.NoProblems: Nothing wrong found: Windows started every function, and the descriptors add up.
UsbProbe.Device.Problem.Strings: The device did not answer every string request; names may be missing. Read device again asks once more.
UsbProbe.Device.Problem.Asleep: The device is selectively suspended (asleep). Read device again wakes it.
UsbProbe.Device.Status.NotFound: No device at '{0}' right now. This page shows it when it is plugged in.
UsbProbe.Device.Status.Failed: Could not read the USB tree: {0}
